classification.difficultyReason: Part a is routine double integration with initial conditions. Part b is the hardest demand. The student must rebuild the equations of motion for new numbers, because the vector r is not handed over for 25 m/s. They then eliminate t, use sec²θ = 1+tan²θ to reach a quadratic in tanθ, and solve it for two angles. This matches p37-q1, which gives r and the target equation, but with slightly less scaffolding. It sits below p38-q4 and p40-q7, which need non-factorising solutions and an unprompted setup.

content.prompt: A particle is projected from the origin at $50\text{ m/s}$ and passes through $(100,25)$. Let $\theta$ be the angle of projection above the horizontal. Use $g=10\text{ m/s}^2$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the displacement vector by integration.

answer.worked:
The acceleration is
$$\underset{\sim}{a}=\begin{pmatrix}0\\-10\end{pmatrix}.$$
Integrating,
$$\underset{\sim}{v}=\begin{pmatrix}C_1\\-10t+C_2\end{pmatrix}.$$
At $t=0$, $\underset{\sim}{v}=\begin{pmatrix}50\cos\theta\\50\sin\theta\end{pmatrix}$, so
$$\underset{\sim}{v}=\begin{pmatrix}50\cos\theta\\-10t+50\sin\theta\end{pmatrix}.$$
Integrating again,
$$\underset{\sim}{r}=\begin{pmatrix}50\cos\theta\,t+D_1\\-5t^2+50\sin\theta\,t+D_2\end{pmatrix}.$$
Since the particle starts at the origin, $D_1=D_2=0$. Thus
$$\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=\begin{pmatrix}50\cos\theta\,t\\-5t^2+50\sin\theta\,t\end{pmatrix}\text{ m}.$$

children.label: b
children.prompt:
A particle is projected from the origin at $25\text{ m/s}$ and passes through $(50,10)$. Let $\theta$ be the angle of projection above the horizontal. Use $g=10\text{ m/s}^2$.

Show that $2\tan^2\theta-5\tan\theta+3=0$ and find both possible angles. Give non-exact angles to $1$ decimal place.

answer.worked:
The equations of motion are
$$\begin{align*}x&=25\cos\theta\,t\\y&=-5t^2+25\sin\theta\,t.\end{align*}$$
At $(50,10)$, from the horizontal equation,
$$\begin{align*}50&=25\cos\theta\,t\\t&=\frac{2}{\cos\theta}.\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the vertical equation with $y=10$:
$$\begin{align*}10&=-5\left(\frac{2}{\cos\theta}\right)^2+25\sin\theta\left(\frac{2}{\cos\theta}\right)\\10&=-20\sec^2\theta+50\tan\theta\\10&=-20(1+\tan^2\theta)+50\tan\theta\\20\tan^2\theta-50\tan\theta+30&=0\\2\tan^2\theta-5\tan\theta+3&=0\\(2\tan\theta-3)(\tan\theta-1)&=0.\end{align*}$$
Hence $\tan\theta=1$ or $\tan\theta=\frac32$, giving
$$\theta=45^\circ\quad\text{or}\quad\theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac32\right)\approx56.3^\circ.$$
